A particular control point in the array is selected for display by using the arrow knobs.The left/right arrows will changed the column index of the control point.The up/down arrows will changed the row index of the control point.The indexing starts at 0.

Kind is a type of metadata that is used to classify prims in USD and determines the selection behavior in the Viewport. Custom strings can be defined for production pipelines. Kind examples:
  • assembly - an important group model, often a published asset or reference to a published asset
  • group - models that simply group other models.
  • component - a 'leaf model' that can contain no other models
  • model - base class for all model kinds. 'model' is considered an abstract type and should not be assigned as any prim's kind.
  • subcomponent - an identified, important 'sub part' of a component model.

Defines a cubic term that affects the radial distortion of the texture applied to the card, and the edges of the card. Positive values make the card rounder, negative make the corners sharper. The lens distort values can be used to simulate camera lens distortion effects, such as barrel distortion.

Defines a square term that affects the radial distortion of the texture applied to the card, and the edges of the card. Positive values make the card rounder, negative make the corners sharper. The lens distort values can be used to simulate camera lens distortion effects, such as barrel distortion.

Defines a linear term that affects the radial distortion of the texture applied to the card, and the edges of the card. Positive values make the card rounder, negative make the corners sharper. The lens distort values can be used to simulate camera lens distortion effects, such as barrel distortion.
This is the focal length of the camera that took the picture on the card. The card is scaled the correct size so that at distance z it fills this field of view.
This is the horizontal aperture of the camera that took the picture on the card. The card is scaled the correct size so that at distance z it fills this field of view.

Set how your prims are displayed within the viewer. Note setting a purpose will override the purpose of its descendants. When purpose is set, the viewport display can be filtered by purpose categories.
  • Default: Assign to prims that have no defined purpose that will generally be included in all renders.
  • Render: Assign to prims intended for final high-quality rendering.
  • Proxy: Assign to prims intended for lightweight proxy rendering.
  • Guide: Assign to prims intended as markings, lines, arrows or interaction guides.

Sets how meshes are rendered in the viewer based on different subdivision models:
  • Catmull Clark: algorithm that smooths the appearance of a mesh using recursive refinement to generate quadrilaterals
  • Bilinear: algorithm that subdivides a mesh without smoothing the appearance
  • None: no subdivision is applied to the mesh
